title: Bill Krisher: OU Guard, 1957 Consensus All-American
question: Who was the Oklahoma guard who became a consensus All-American in 1957 and an AFL All-Star?
answer: Bill Krisher, a guard from Midwest City who played for Bud Wilkinson from 1955 to 1957, was a consensus All-American in 1957. He later played for the Dallas Texans of the AFL and was a two-time AFL All-Star.
summary: Bill Krisher, a Midwest City lineman, helped OU win national titles in 1955 and 1956, earned 1957 consensus All-America honors and became an AFL All-Star.
body: Bill Krisher, sometimes called Billy in news coverage, grew up in Midwest City and chose Oklahoma over interest from Oklahoma A&M and Notre Dame. He played for Bud Wilkinson from 1955 through 1957, lining up as an offensive guard even though he weighed only about 216 pounds.

He arrived just as Oklahoma was at its peak. The Sooners won national championships in 1955 and 1956, and Krisher was part of the Wilkinson era's famous winning streak, which came to an end in 1957 with a 7-0 loss to Notre Dame.

Honors followed his play. Krisher was a third-team All-American in 1956 and a consensus All-American in 1957, and he was a first-team All-Big Eight selection both seasons. Coverage of his Hall of Fame selection described him as only the third Oklahoma player to be a two-time All-American.

The Pittsburgh Steelers drafted him in the third round in 1958, 32nd overall. After a season in Pittsburgh he joined the Dallas Texans of the new American Football League, where he was All-AFL in 1960 and an AFL All-Star in 1960 and 1961. That franchise later became the Kansas City Chiefs.

Away from the field, Krisher was active in the Fellowship of Christian Athletes and later worked as one of its regional leaders. He was inducted into the Oklahoma Sports Hall of Fame in 2017, and The Oklahoman ranked him No. 50 on its 2019 list of the greatest Sooners. News outlets reported his death in Dallas in late July 2025 at age 89.
